Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea MATE_ARITMETIC_RESTA_1_DIGITO`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Restas de un dígito*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/MATE_ARITMETIC_RESTA_1_DIGITO.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Single-digit subtraction, from age 6 to 7 (482 administrations in 2 cohorts). ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 10760 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 40 (10760) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | INSTRUCCIONES En esta tarea vas a hacer de profe. Vas a ver unas restas que han realizado otros niños y niñas. *(Spanish)* | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |-----:|:--------------------|:---------------------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:----------|------------------:| | 10760|Restas |Estímulo y opciones en pantalla; autoaplicada | 40| 0|— |60 s |fijo |Eficiencia | 6.2, 7.2| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **10760.** 40 restas con resultado (verificar), 60 s; autoaplicada. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![10760 · Restas](../../figuras/plataforma/10760.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 10760"} ::: ## Theoretical framework These tasks measure **arithmetic fluency**: solving simple additions and subtractions quickly, above all by retrieving arithmetic facts from memory. There are two formats. In the **production** formats (ages 6–8), the child says the result aloud and the examiner records it. In the **verification** formats (codes 107xx, school year 2021/22), the child sees the operation with a result and decides whether it is correct; they are self-administered and time-limited (60 or 120 s). **What the evidence says:** - **Producing and verifying are not exactly the same.** Production and verification errors are primed separately: verification relies more on the familiarity of the presented result [@campbell1996retrieval]. Scores from the two formats are not interchangeable. - **Arithmetic and reading fluency share predictors.** In 200 Finnish children followed from age 5 to 10, counting and RAN predicted both calculation and reading fluency [@koponen2013counting]. A common factor of RAN and verbal counting was the best predictor of what the two fluencies share [@koponen2020serial]. - **Phonological awareness is associated with fact retrieval, not with procedural calculation.** In 63 children with learning difficulties, phonemic awareness was related to problems solved from memory and not to those that require counting [@matejko2022phonological]. - **Difficulties are persistent and can be anticipated in preschool.** In 2,518 Finnish children followed from Grade 1 to Grade 9, 12% had persistent arithmetic fluency difficulties; preschool counting, number concepts and RAN distinguished this profile [@psyridou2023profiles]. **What our data show.** - **Production.** One-digit additions and two-digit additions and subtractions have acceptable consistency (α = .72–.76). They predict low arithmetic at ages 10–11 (AUC .59–.71) and, to the same extent, low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (AUC .67–.74). The two-digit version has a ceiling at age 7 (23–33% maximum scores) and its screen shows a result, although the instructions ask the child to solve: which format was administered needs to be confirmed. - **Verification.** We do not yet have α for these versions. Their relation with concurrent low reading fluency is moderate (AUC .58–.69). The task for ages 10–11 (code 10748) is itself the low-arithmetic criterion ([Numerical cognition](../../cognicion-numerica.en.qmd#sec-mate-criterio)) and cannot be validated against it. - **Comorbidity.** Of 799 children aged 10–11, 19 have both low arithmetic and low reading, compared with 12.3 expected by chance. Together with the above, this supports a shared retrieval fluency. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.2| 2015| 950|2021/22 | 226| 0| 24| 8| | 7.1| 2014| 950|2021/22 | 256| 0| 0| 8| ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (6.2, r = .14); Reading comprehension (7.1, r = .16). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|----:| | 6.2| 226| 2015| 0| 2.0| 4| 5| 8| 10| 17.5| | 7.1| 256| 2014| 0| 4.5| 7| 8| 11| 15| 19.0| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_ARITMETIC_RESTA_1_DIGITO_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 219| -0.342| 0.012| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 224| 0.094| 0.159| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 226| 0.038| | |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 253| -0.176| 0.160| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 253| 0.020| 0.755| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 256| 0.000| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Single-digit subtraction” (code 10760; LEEDUCA battery) assesses arithmetic. The examiner presents each item orally, supported by a picture on the screen, and records the child's oral response. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 2 sessions, from 6 to 7 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
